question: An engineer configures user authentication on Cisco UCS Manager to ensure that the user and roles can be saved on the external server and secured using authentication. Which set of actions meets these requirements?
options: Implement a logical configuration backup and configure the HTTPS protocol.
Configure a full state backup and implement an FTP protocol.
Perform a system configuration backup and use the SCP protocol.
Deploy an all configuration backup and implement a TFTP protocol.
theory: Cisco UCS Manager offers several distinct backup types; a system configuration backup captures the logical configuration - including local users, roles, and AAA settings - separately from a full-state binary backup, making it the appropriate choice when the goal is to preserve users/roles on an external server. Pairing it with SCP (which requires authenticated, encrypted transport) rather than FTP or TFTP (both unauthenticated/unencrypted) satisfies the requirement that the backup transfer itself be secured. (Cisco UCS Manager Administration Management Guide / general Cisco documentation - Backup Types)
